proposals.citation: CDIAL[6328];webster[Appendix B, printed p. 47 (PDF p. 52), item 117, KkP]
proposals.evidence: CDIAL dina supplies regional din “day, daytime”. The same surveyed language independently attests dīn “day” (f_nbjkgaxhh2umu), supporting the local day/sun polysemy rather than choosing a remote sun root by sound alone. The source’s sun gloss, vowel length and dental/retroflex spelling are retained. This identifies the day-word family and leaves possible intra-Indo-Aryan transmission open.
